# Tessl fixture: tutors-sdk/tutors

A real-world Tessl consumer project, vendored so the importer is exercised
against the layout Tessl actually writes rather than a synthetic sample.

- Source: <https://github.com/tutors-sdk/tutors>
- Commit: `3f578d9362e6d1d0148b15665a534e335df90dc1`
- License: MIT (see `LICENSE`)

Vendored from that commit:

- `in/tessl.json` — the consumer manifest. It lists twenty `tessl/<name>`
  dependencies and no `mode`; a dependency that is not on disk stays
  needs-action.
- `in/.tessl/RULES.md` — generated by `tessl install`; dropped, not imported.
  Upstream writes its link with Windows separators; they were normalised to `/`
  so `poly lint` accepts the file (the link target is unchanged).
- `in/.tessl/tiles/tessl/cli-setup/` — one vendored tile in the consumer layout:
  `tile.json` (rules under a `steering` map) plus its `steering/` rule. Only this
  one tile is vendored, so the nineteen other listed dependencies are reported
  needs-action; `cli-setup` itself is not listed in `tessl.json` and is still
  imported.

`want/` is the golden tree `ai-rulez convert` writes for `in/`. Regenerate it
after an intended change with:

```sh
UPDATE_GOLDEN=1 go test ./internal/importer -run TestConvert_GoldenRealFixtures
```
